title: Nightly web error check, line by line
subtitle: Every path through the log checker: read the log, count failures per endpoint, write a report, email on-call above 5%.

analyze_logs.py:2.title: Import the standard library
analyze_logs.py:2.text: Everything comes from the standard library: re for parsing, Counter for tallies, json for the report, smtplib and EmailMessage for the alert.

analyze_logs.py:9.title: Define the settings
analyze_logs.py:9.text: Paths, the alert threshold (5% of requests) and the mail settings, as module constants.

analyze_logs.py:15.title: Compile the log-line pattern once
analyze_logs.py:15.text: re.compile at import time avoids recompiling for every line. Named groups (?P<name>...) let groupdict() return a dict keyed by field name.

analyze_logs.py:68.title: Run main() when executed as a script
analyze_logs.py:68.text: Arguments from the command line are unpacked into main(), so an optional path argument overrides LOG_PATH.

analyze_logs.py:56.title: Open the log file
analyze_logs.py:56.text: The with block guarantees the file is closed even if parsing fails. fh is a lazy line iterator; nothing is read yet.

analyze_logs.py:57.title: Parse and summarise in one pass
analyze_logs.py:57.text: parse(fh) is a generator, so this builds a pipeline: summarize pulls one parsed request at a time, and parse reads one line at a time. The whole log is never held in memory.

analyze_logs.py:34.title: Start two counters
analyze_logs.py:34.text: Counter is a dict subclass whose missing keys read as 0, so += 1 works without initialising each endpoint.

analyze_logs.py:35.title: Consume the parsed requests
analyze_logs.py:35.text: Each iteration resumes the parse generator until it yields the next request dict.

analyze_logs.py:36.title: Normalise the path
analyze_logs.py:36.text: Collapses ids so /orders/123 and /orders/456 count as the same endpoint.

analyze_logs.py:38.title: Count server errors
analyze_logs.py:38.text: Status 500 and above is a server-side failure; 4xx client errors are deliberately not counted.

analyze_logs.py:40.title: Build one row per endpoint
analyze_logs.py:40.text: most_common() orders endpoints by request count. errors[ep] is 0 for endpoints without failures, thanks to Counter.

analyze_logs.py:20.title: Iterate over the raw lines
analyze_logs.py:20.text: Iterating a file object yields one line at a time, including its trailing newline.

analyze_logs.py:21.title: Match the line
analyze_logs.py:21.text: search returns a Match object or None. Lines that don't fit the pattern, such as garbage or truncated writes, produce None.

analyze_logs.py:22.title: Skip lines that didn't match
analyze_logs.py:22.text: Only matched lines are turned into records; the rest are dropped silently, which hides how much of the log was unreadable.

analyze_logs.py:24.title: Convert the status to an integer
analyze_logs.py:24.text: groupdict values are strings; the numeric comparison later needs an int.

analyze_logs.py:25.title: Hand one record to the consumer
analyze_logs.py:25.text: yield suspends parse here and returns d to summarize's for loop; execution resumes on the next line when the next item is requested.

analyze_logs.py:62.title: Compute the overall failure rate
analyze_logs.py:62.text: The conditional expression guards against an empty log, where total would be 0.

analyze_logs.py:63.title: Alert above the threshold
analyze_logs.py:63.text: Compares the night's failure rate with ERROR_RATE_ALERT (0.05). The email is only sent above 5%.

analyze_logs.py:49.title: Pick the five worst endpoints
analyze_logs.py:49.text: sorted with a key function and reverse=True orders by error count, highest first; the slice keeps the top five.

analyze_logs.py:51.title: Connect to the mail server
analyze_logs.py:51.text: smtplib.SMTP opens the connection in its constructor; as a context manager it sends QUIT on exit.
